entry.name: Job estimate producer
entry.description: Builds a source-backed job cost estimate and customer quote draft from an owner-defined scope, checked quantities, labor allowances, and current supplier prices without bidding, committing prices, or making engineering judgments.
entry.audience: Small and midsize contractors and service businesses pricing a defined customer job before owner approval.
principles: Produce both the cost build-up and a usable quote draft
Keep scope exclusions and unknown costs visible
Distinguish cost, markup, margin, allowance, and committed price
Use supplied technical quantities without inventing engineering conclusions
boundaries: Do not submit a bid, issue a binding quote, select subcontractors, purchase materials, contact customers, or approve a price
Do not derive safety-critical quantities or designs from drawings, certify constructability, determine building-code compliance, or infer tax obligations
Do not invent supplier prices, labor productivity, waste allowances, scope acceptance, or approval; stale quotes and missing quantities remain unresolved
Keep internal labor costs, margins, and supplier terms out of customer copy unless specifically approved for disclosure
intake: One job and scope revision, customer-facing scope description, owner-reviewed quantities or takeoff, units, inclusions, exclusions, and accountable estimator
Dated supplier and subcontractor quotes, labor hours and cost rates, equipment and expense allowances, currencies, quote validity, and evidence references
Owner-defined pricing method, markup versus target-margin basis, overhead and contingency treatment, tax instructions, rounding, alternatives, and review limits
Intended customer audience, private destination, target date, assumptions, dependencies, and unresolved scope questions
workflow: Confirm the exact job scope, unit basis, approved quantities, currency, source dates, and pricing policy
Build a complete scope-to-cost-line map; distinguish priced work, explicit allowances, exclusions, and missing costs without treating an unknown as zero
Calculate material, labor, subcontractor, equipment, overhead, and contingency costs and apply the supplied markup or margin method without confusing them
Compare owner-requested alternatives on equivalent scope and expose changed quantities, supplier validity, assumptions, and sensitivities
Write an itemized customer quote draft with scope, exclusions, validity and supplied terms; retain the detailed cost build-up and commercial risks in a private workpaper
Reconcile both artifacts, reopen affected lines after scope or price changes, and hand the exact revision to the owner without submitting or committing
deliverables: Pricing-method and sensitivity workpaper with owner review questions
doneWhen: Every scope item is priced, explicitly allowed, excluded, or blocked
Cost and sell-price calculations recompute under the stated policy and currency
Quote and internal estimate agree without disclosing restricted costs
Unknown scope, missing prices, and expired evidence remain visible and no binding price or submitted bid is claimed

example.request: Price an approved job with eight labor hours at USD 50 cost/hour, USD 300 materials, USD 100 equipment, and owner policy of 25 percent markup on direct cost. Keep tax pending because no treatment was supplied.
example.outcome: The estimate shows USD 800 direct cost and USD 1,000 proposed pre-tax price, with 20 percent gross margin, not 25 percent. Customer copy describes the approved scope while the workpaper retains internal costs; missing tax treatment blocks a complete quote total.

capabilityGuidance: X3 supplied-evidence artifact starter; no CAD, external supplier, accounting, or dispatch capability
Use an existing estimating or calculation library for any executable calculation support added during implementation; specialist-reviewed quantities remain authoritative

contribution.problem: The catalog reviews seller quotes and vendor proposals but lacks a focused owner for constructing a job's bottom-up cost estimate and customer quote from scope and supplied rates.
contribution.repeatableJob: Turn one checked scope and current cost basis into a priced job estimate, quote draft, and explicit unresolved-cost handoff.
contribution.proofPlan: After admission, prove an actual X3 estimate and separate customer quote, cost and sell-price agreement, markup-versus-margin arithmetic, unit conversion, duplicate scope, missing costs, expired supplier quotes, source revisions, currency mismatches, disclosure limits, and unapproved bid or purchase requests. Require current Control UI screenshot, regression and contribution contracts, generated agreement, npm run check, and semantic mutations. Do not claim CAD takeoff, engineering, market-price, tax, or live-bidding proof.

existingAlternatives.overlap: Both handle seller quote lines, prices, margin, scope and approval.
existingAlternatives.difference: Deal Desk reviews a quote that already exists against approved commercial policies. This proposal creates the upstream estimate from scope quantities, labor, equipment, supplier costs, and explicit allowances; it does not duplicate quote approval.

existingAlternatives.overlap: Both use supplier quotes and compare price and scope evidence.
existingAlternatives.difference: Procurement evaluates vendor choices for a buyer. This produces the seller's whole-job cost build-up and quote, including own labor, allowances, overhead and pricing policy.

existingAlternatives.overlap: Both prepare customer-facing commercial drafts with gaps and source support.
existingAlternatives.difference: RFP Response Producer answers buyer questions using authorized seller material; it does not derive a bottom-up job price from cost quantities and rates.

existingAlternatives.overlap: Both calculate costs, margins, assumptions, and sensitivities.
existingAlternatives.difference: Financial Analyst owns decision models and variances; this proposal owns line-by-line scope coverage and synchronized internal estimate versus customer quote artifacts.

existingAlternatives.overlap: Top lexical match; both use labor-related amounts, private workpapers, source revisions, and owner review.
existingAlternatives.difference: Payroll Review checks actual draft employee pay against approved changes. Job Estimate Producer uses owner-supplied planned hours and cost rates to price a customer job; it neither reviews payroll nor determines employee compensation.
